findings.title: Password rule leaves noncharacters and Private Use open to divergent readings
findings.reproduction: Compare 'normalization MUST fail if P contains a code point unassigned in Unicode 17.0.0' with UAX #15 revision 57, section 12.1, and with the Unicode glossary.
findings.expected: One reading: NPSS fails on General_Category=Unassigned (Cn), which includes the 66 noncharacters, and accepts Private Use (Co).
findings.observed: The README says 'unassigned'; in the Unicode glossary that means reserved and excludes noncharacters. The common Rust helper is_public_assigned rejects Private Use, and the reference implementation needed an explicit exception. The vector requirements name neither case.
findings.impact: Two implementations could disagree on whether a rare password is valid, making a container unrecoverable across them.
findings.recommendedFix: Write the condition as General_Category=Unassigned (Cn) in Unicode 17.0.0, noting that noncharacters are rejected and Private Use accepted; add a noncharacter and a Private Use vector.
findings.requiredVerification: Reread against UAX #15 section 12.1; the suite 3 vectors contain both cases.

findings.title: Container self-check is SHOULD, but programmatic release requires it to pass
findings.reproduction: Read step 5 ('This SHOULD be done') and 'A result passed to another program instead of a person MUST NOT be released before the check has passed.'
findings.observed: An implementation that skips the SHOULD-level check can never meet the MUST, so the check is mandatory in effect for programs while the step calls it optional.
findings.impact: Implementers may disagree on whether the check is required.
findings.recommendedFix: Make step 5 a MUST, as the reference implementation already behaves, or limit the release rule to implementations that perform the check.
findings.requiredVerification: Reread the section; CHANGELOG.md states the same strength.

findings.title: Intermediate round salts are described as public
findings.reproduction: Follow the inverse diagram: only S_11 is computable from the container (R_11 = L_12) and S_0 from a known original; every other S_i depends on R_i, which the ciphertext-only argument treats as hidden.
findings.expected: The text says which salts are derivable from public data and lists intermediate salts and masks among sensitive values.
findings.observed: README: 'The salt is computed from public data'; supplement: 'State-derived salts are public ... It is also not secret'; the sensitive-memory list omits salts and masks.
findings.impact: An implementer could log or export intermediate salts as harmless; one leaked intermediate salt allows a one-Argon2id-call filter per guess. No leaking implementation path is known.
findings.recommendedFix: Qualify the salt sentence (only the first salt of a recovery or of an encryption is derivable from public data), add salts and masks to Sensitive memory, forbid logging or exporting intermediate states, salts, keys and masks outside public-data test vectors, and retitle the Part II heading.

findings.title: Undefined symbol N in 'a discount of 1/N'
findings.reproduction: Search the symbol table and nearby text for N.
findings.observed: N appears only in 'a discount of 1/N'; nearby text uses N1 and N2 for counts of passwords and passphrases.
findings.impact: Minor confusion with N1 and N2.
findings.recommendedFix: Write 'a discount of one twelfth' or define N as the number of rounds.

findings.title: Supplement bound 'never more than sixteen' contradicts its own formula
findings.observed: 'never more than sixteen with a range of 0..31'.
findings.impact: A wrong bound in non-normative text.
findings.recommendedFix: Write 'at most about sixteen' or 'at most 16.5'.

findings.title: Changelog 0.3.1 entry nests two independent changes as sub-items
findings.reproduction: Render the 0.3.1 entry or read its indentation.
findings.observed: 'added implementation requirements...' is indented four spaces and 'switched the header to the BIP 3 preamble...' six, so they render as sub-items.
findings.recommendedFix: Indent both items like their siblings and rewrap.
findings.requiredVerification: Prettier check and a rendered view.

observations.title: Reference [7] pairs BIP 3 version 1.4.0 with the assignment date
observations.reproduction: Compare reference [7] with BIP 3's preamble and changelog.
observations.observed: 'ver. 1.4.0, Jan. 9, 2025': 1.4.0 is dated 2025-12-09; Jan. 9, 2025 is the assignment date.

observations.title: Reference [42] omits 'Deep Dive:' from the article title
observations.reproduction: Compare reference [42] with the EFF article.
observations.observed: The article is titled 'Deep Dive: EFF's New Wordlists for Random Passphrases'.

observations.title: Part II asks readers to apply suite 2 text to suite 3 next to suite 2 formulas
observations.reproduction: Read the supplement introduction and Part II's salt formula.
observations.expected: Historical formulas are clearly labelled as suite 2.
observations.observed: The introduction says to read 'suite 2' in Part II as 'the current suite' unless Part I says otherwise; Part II keeps the salt message without BE32(MEM) and PIM 0..31. The introduction does list the differences.
observations.impact: Small risk of copying a suite 2 formula.
observations.recommendedFix: Label Part II formulas as suite 2 formulas.
